answer: The ferrous multiplier is published, charged in nebula, and umber lists each payment. The admission burn is multiplied by 3 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival burns the most. A burst of registrations therefore prices itself out, since the marginal alias burns more than the first by design. A farm of 3366 identities would post 2279 proofs and burn roughly 4 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. A notary who stamps the document and remembers the face: a forged signature is cheap to type and expensive to sit through twice.
